MUQATIL:18:13-17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r1.claim: The youths believed by affirming God's oneness, and God increased their guidance when they separated from their people.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r6.claim: God tells the Prophet their story truthfully; the youths' increased guidance means increased faith.

TUSTARI:18:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:13/r1.claim: They are called youths because they believed in God without an intermediary and approached Him after shedding their attachments.

TUSTARI:18:13/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:13/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:13/r2.claim: The increase in guidance means increased insight in faith.

TAB-FULL:v15p178/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p178/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p178/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad the truthful account of the youths who took refuge in the cave after the Meccan pagans asked about them; they believed in their Lord.

TAB-FULL:v15p178/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p178/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p178/r2.claim: God increased their faith and insight, enabling them to endure leaving home and comfortable life for hardship in the cave to preserve their religion.

NAHHAS:v2p450/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p450/r1.claim: Fitya is a nonproductive plural of fatā used for a small number; the usual larger plural is fityān.

SULAMI:v1p403/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p403/r1.claim: Their increased guidance was added light, so powerful that the sun shifted from their cave lest their light extinguish its own.

SULAMI:v1p403/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r10.speaker: الفضيل
SULAMI:v1p403/r10.claim: Futuwwa is forgiving the lapses of one's brethren.

SULAMI:v1p403/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p403/r2.claim: The story is told truthfully so that God may look upon them through direct witnessing.

SULAMI:v1p403/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p403/r3.claim: Their increased guidance means insight into faith.

SULAMI:v1p403/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p403/r4.claim: They were called youths because they believed without an intermediary and approached God after shedding worldly attachments.

SULAMI:v1p403/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p403/r5.claim: The first step of faith is futuwwa: remaining unaltered by whatever states arrive.

SULAMI:v1p403/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r6.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
SULAMI:v1p403/r6.claim: Futuwwa is the tongue affirming promise and warning, with outward and inward states matching as true faith requires.

SULAMI:v1p403/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r7.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p403/r7.claim: Futuwwa means viewing all people with the regard of saints and excusing rather than blaming them for sins.

SULAMI:v1p403/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p403/r8.claim: Futuwwa means not caring to whom one offers generosity, provided it is accepted.

SULAMI:v1p403/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p403/r9.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p403/r9.claim: Futuwwa is following sacred law and prophetic practice, with broadness of heart and good character.

THALABI:v6p158/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r1.claim: The Qur'an recounts and reveals the true report about the cave companions.

THALABI:v6p158/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r2.claim: They are called youths because they were young men who believed; the author says God granted them that description upon believing without intermediary.

THALABI:v6p158/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r3.speaker: أهل اللسان
THALABI:v6p158/r3.claim: The language scholars say faith is the foundation of futuwwa.

THALABI:v6p158/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r4.speaker: الجنيد
THALABI:v6p158/r4.claim: Al-Junayd defines futuwwa as refraining from harm, giving generously, and not complaining.

THALABI:v6p158/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r5.claim: One definition says futuwwa consists of avoiding forbidden acts and practicing noble deeds.

THALABI:v6p158/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r6.claim: Another definition says a youth neither claims virtue before acting nor praises himself after acting.

THALABI:v6p158/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r7.claim: A saying distinguishes spiritual courage from merely enduring lashes: the true youth is one who crosses the bridge.

THALABI:v6p158/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r8.claim: Another saying defines true youth by feeding the poor rather than merely enduring the knife.

THALABI:v6p158/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r9.claim: God increases the youths in guidance by increasing their faith, insight, and certainty.

QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r6.claim: One explanation calls them youths because they believed immediately when the summons to union reached them.

QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r7.claim: Another explanation calls them youths because they stood for God and did not settle until they reached Him.

QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r8.claim: God gently brought them, disclosed their secrets with added lights, and raised them from clarification to certainty.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r1.claim: The account of the youths is true; they were young men, and God increased their guidance by keeping them steadfast.

JISHUMI:v6p4363/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r2.claim: Qaṣaṣ is a report whose parts follow one another, from the root of following a trace; the same sense appears in the command to follow Moses' sister's trail.

JISHUMI:v6p4363/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r3.claim: Fitya is an irregular plural of fatā, unlike the more regular pairs ghulām/ghilma and ṣabī/ṣabiya.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r1.claim: The account is true; the youths believed in their Lord and received increased faith and insight.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661/r1.claim: God increased their guidance through granting success and steadfastness.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.claim: After the dispute over which group best counted the duration, God says that He recounts their true story; these verses answer Quraysh's questions prompted by the Israelites.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.claim: Qass means reporting a connected, unfolding account, rather than reproducing a conversation word for word.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#3/r3.claim: Increasing their guidance means enabling righteous action, devotion, separation from people, and renunciation of worldly life, additions to their faith.

TABRISI:18:13-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:13-14/r6.claim: The kasra in innahum fitya begins a new sentence; idh qāmū is attached to ‘We strengthened,’ and shataṭan is a verbal noun.

TABRISI:18:13-14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:13-14/r7.claim: God calls them youths because they believed and increased in insight and desire to remain firm through gracious assistance that strengthened their commitment.

TABRISI:18:13-14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:18:13-14/r8.claim: Mujāhid defines futuwwa as generosity, refraining from harm, and not complaining.

TABRISI:18:13-14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:13-14/r9.claim: Another definition of futuwwa is avoiding forbidden things and practicing noble conduct.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p115/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p115/r1.claim: The report of the youths is told truthfully.

RAZI-FULL:v21p83#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p83#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p83#2/r1.claim: The opening says God recounts the youths' true account: they were a group of young men who believed in God.

RAZI-FULL:v21p83#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p83#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p83#2/r2.claim: “We strengthened their hearts” means God inspired patience and made them steadfast.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r1.claim: After noting disagreement about the youths' duration, God states that He recounts their true story and knows its actual course.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r2.speaker: أهل اللسان
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r2.claim: The youths are called young men, and linguistic authorities say faith is the foundation of futuwwa.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r3.speaker: الجنيد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r3.claim: Al-Junayd defines futuwwa as giving generously, refraining from harm, and not complaining.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r4.claim: Another definition is avoiding forbidden things and hastening to virtuous acts; al-Qurtubi prefers it as encompassing the other definitions.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r5.claim: Their increased guidance means God made righteous action easy for them, including devoting themselves to God, avoiding people, and renouncing worldly life; this adds to faith.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r6.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:13/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says God increased their guidance through the shepherd's dog: after they chased it, it prayed, spoke of knowing God forty years before them, and they were guided further.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r5.claim: The account is true, and the youths' faith was strengthened by God's confirmation and support.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r1.claim: The account is true; فتية is the plural of fatā. Futuwwa means generosity, refraining from harm and complaint, avoiding forbidden acts, and practicing virtues.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r2.claim: Another definition says a youth does not claim virtue before acting or praise himself after acting.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r3.claim: God increased their guidance as certainty; they were close associates of Diqyanus, and God placed faith in their hearts.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#3/r4.claim: Afraid to disclose faith in a group, they paired off, each pair privately revealing its belief, and then discovered their agreement.

QASHANI:18:13-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:13-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:13-15/r1.claim: The youths believed with certainty through inference or unveiling, and God increased their guidance toward direct certainty and witnessing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r3.claim: After لنعلم signals disagreement about the youths, نحن نقص presents God’s truthful account piece by piece and parallels لنعلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r4.claim: The word ربهم marks the youths as owned dependents of their master and guardian, rather than merely saying they believed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r5.claim: God’s increase in guidance means enabling righteous action, devotion, distance from people, and worldly renunciation; it increases the faith they already had.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r6.claim: Al-Taḥrīr offers two meanings for increased guidance: its fruits or certainty.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r7.claim: Al-Taḥrīr lists obedience and avoiding prohibitions as one means by which guidance increased.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r8.claim: One explanation says the dog’s speech confirmed to the youths that it shared their faith.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r9.claim: Another explanation says an angel reassured the youths and foretold an Arab prophet who would make the religion wholly God’s; they believed before his mission.

SAMIN-DURR:18:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:13/r1.claim: آمنوا بربهم shifts from first-person speech to third person; consistent wording would be آمنوا بنا.

SAMIN-DURR:18:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:13/r2.claim: وزدناهم and وربطنا then shift from third person back to first-person speech.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r1.claim: The youths were young, and young people are more receptive to truth than elders hardened in false religion; most early responders to God and His Messenger were young, while most Quraysh elders remained unbelievers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r2.claim: Mujahid says he heard that some youths wore earrings, and God inspired their guidance and gave them piety.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r3.claim: Their faith meant acknowledging God's oneness and that none is worthy of worship except Him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r4.claim: Bukhari and other imams cite the increase in the youths' guidance as evidence that faith grows and diminishes, alongside 47:17, 9:124, and 48:4.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p140/r5.claim: Although some say the youths followed Jesus, Ibn Kathir thinks they likely lived before Christianity, since Jewish scholars preserved their story; Quraysh asked them about the youths, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, showing the story predated Christianity.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r1.claim: God recounts the story in detail and truthfully, unlike other tellings that may add to or omit from it.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r2.claim: The youths believed in their Lord, who created and provided for them and endowed them with sound, useful reason.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p449/r3.claim: After their initial faith, God increased their guidance by granting knowledge and opening their hearts, enabling sacrifice and renunciation of worldly life.

DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.claim: The sleepers were Muslim sons of kings who fled their people's religion and withdrew to the cave; they remained asleep until their people died and a Muslim generation arose under a Muslim king.

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says prophets were sent while young and knowledge was granted to people while young, citing Abraham, Moses, and the Cave youths as examples.

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r7.claim: The increase in guidance means increased sincerity.

BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r6.claim: ‘We narrate’ means explain their story; ‘in truth’ qualifies an omitted verbal noun, since storytellers distort accounts to suit their temper and desire, and only God narrates truly.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r1.speaker: التكملة
BURSEVI:v5p171/r1.claim: A disciple of Jesus refused to bow at the city idol, worked in a nearby bath, and taught local youths until they believed; after the king’s son and a woman died in the bath, the disciple fled and the youths escaped to the cave.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p171/r2.claim: The author thinks they were moved to faith by heavenly inspiration and divine attraction without an evidentiary argument, as the Najmiyya commentary suggests.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
BURSEVI:v5p171/r3.claim: Some say they lived before Jesus, who told people their story, and awoke after his ascension during the interval before Muhammad.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r4.speaker: الطبري
BURSEVI:v5p171/r4.claim: Another account places them after Jesus as Christians; al-Tabari says this is the view of most scholars.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p171/r5.claim: God increased their guidance by establishing them firmly in true religion and revealing its hidden beauties.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p171/r6.claim: They are called fityan because their faith was verified rather than imitated; they sought guidance from God through God, initially within their own understanding and capacity.

BURSEVI:v5p171/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p171/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p171/r7.claim: God exceeded their hoped-for guidance: after 309 years they awoke with bodies and clothes unchanged, so faith became certainty and the unseen became direct vision.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r1.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r1.claim: Al-Kashf cites Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt to argue that Arabs knew of the cave story, though they did not know it accurately.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others describe Christians whose community had become sinful and idolatrous under tyrants, while a remnant still followed Jesus and worshipped one God.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r3.claim: The king called Daqyanus or Daqyus persecuted Christians, offering death or idol worship and displaying the bodies of believers he killed.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r4.claim: The youths were prominent residents of Ephesus or Tarsus; they were arrested while praying, confessed one God before the king, and their eldest, Mکسlimina, spoke first.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r5.claim: The king stripped their fine clothes and delayed punishment because they were young, giving them time to reconsider while he left for Nineveh.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r6.claim: After agreeing to flee, each youth took money from his family, gave some away, and carried the rest to a nearby cave called Banjalus.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216#2/r7.claim: They prayed and fasted in the cave; Yumlikha secretly bought supplies and gathered news until the returning king sought them, after which they prostrated and fell asleep with their dog.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r1.claim: The passage begins unpacking the story previously summarized: God now recounts its significant details to the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r2.claim: Al-haqq may modify an omitted verbal noun, function circumstantially for the subject of “We recount,” or qualify their report circumstantially.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r3.claim: A further parse makes al-haqq qualify nabāʾ by omitting a relative pronoun, for grammarians who allow deleting it with part of its clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p216/r4.claim: The author suggests that “with truth” may allude to people in the Prophet's time recounting their story inaccurately.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r1.claim: When the king could not enter the cave, an adviser proposed walling it up so the youths would die of hunger and thirst, and the king did so.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the youths met by chance while fleeing an idol-worshipping king, concealed their reasons, pledged to share them, then united in confessing God and entered the cave.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r3.claim: Their families searched after they disappeared; the king ordered their names written on a lead tablet kept in his treasury.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the youths worked as money changers.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r5.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih recounts a follower of Jesus who avoided a city's gate idol, worked in a bathhouse, and brought selected youths to faith through teaching about heaven and the afterlife.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r6.claim: In Wahb's account, the ruler's son died in the bathhouse with a woman after being rebuked; the converts fled with a fellow farmer, slept in a cave, and were walled in when the king's men could not enter.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r7.claim: The narratives differ, and no sound hadith explains how the youths met or left; the account to rely on is the Quranic description.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r8.claim: “They were youths” resumes the story as an answer to an implied question and echoes the earlier discussion of the word futiyya.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p217/r9.claim: Their faith in their Lord means faith in their master and guardian; the shift to third person highlights that lordship caused their belief and later declaration.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r1.claim: Their guidance increased through steadfastness in faith, success in righteous action, turning wholly to God, and asceticism toward worldly life.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r2.speaker: التحرير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r2.claim: Al-Tahrir gives two interpretations of the increase: the fruits of guidance or increased certainty.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r3.speaker: التحرير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r3.claim: Al-Tahrir says the increase came either through obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions or through the dog affirming their faith, an angel's reassurance, and news of an Arab prophet whose mission they accepted before his call.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r4.claim: An angel's reported visit does not entail that the youths were prophets.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p218/r5.claim: The verb “We increased” shifts from third to first person, magnifying the importance of the increase.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r10.claim: Their belief is intellectual faith; the increase in guidance means God made them present with Him and unveiled realities to them.

ELMALILI:18:13-14/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:13-14/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:13-14/r1.claim: Fitya is the plural of fetā, meaning a young man, lad, or brave youth, and is a plural of paucity.

ELMALILI:18:13-14/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:13-14/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:13-14/r2.claim: Names, exact number, and homeland are not needed for the exemplary truth of the story; their defining traits matter.

ELMALILI:18:13-14/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:13-14/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:13-14/r3.claim: The youths believed in their Lord, and God increased their guidance.

TABATABAI:18:23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:23/r3.claim: The opening verses imply that the cave story was already generally known before revelation, while revelation supplies its details beginning with the truthful account.

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq says the Cave youths were mature men called young because of their faith; another report attributed to Ibn Abbas says they were literally youths.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.claim: The cave story circulated in detailed reports from al-Qummī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, among others.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.claim: The transmitted accounts disagree even on major features, while reports about dates, rulers, lineage, appearance, names, and the title أصحاب الرقيم diverge still more.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.claim: One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.claim: A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.claim: The Qurʾān selects key lessons that serve guidance instead of supplying a complete historical account; it is a book of guidance, not history.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.claim: The Qurʾān omits names, ancestry, birth, upbringing, occupations, social standing, dates, rulers, cities, persecutors, and the dog’s identity because guidance does not depend on them; historians and early exegetes filled these gaps, producing divergent accounts.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r2.claim: The youths lived amid idol worship and were persecuted for their informed monotheistic faith; God increased their guidance, knowledge, and wisdom and strengthened their hearts against fear.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.speaker: أهل الرواية والتاريخ
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.claim: Most historians date the story between Jesus and Muḥammad; it is absent from the two Testaments, though some Muslim reports say Quraysh heard it from Jews, while Christians preserved it extensively.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.claim: Christian accounts resemble Ibn Isḥāq’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās in some respects but differ from Muslims on the number of sleepers, whether they had a dog, and the length of their sleep.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.claim: After centuries as a ruined, forgotten site, Jordanian excavation uncovered Rujayb; the author considers its archaeological signs and some Muslim reports the strongest fit for the Qurʾānic cave.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.claim: Amman stands on the site of Philadelphia, a major and beautiful city before Islam that remained under Roman control from the early second century until the Muslim conquest.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.claim: Other proposed locations include a cave on Mount Qāsiyūn near Damascus, one at Petra, a Scandinavian cave with seven uncorrupted Roman-looking bodies, and a cave near Nakhchivan.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.claim: No evidence identifies any proposed cave as the Qurʾānic one; the Scandinavian and Caucasus claims conflict with the story’s Roman setting and the limits of Roman power.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r5.claim: Their faith was pleasing to God, since otherwise God would not have ascribed it to them.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r6.claim: Their increased guidance means that faith rose toward what leads to God's pleasure, as also described in 57:28.

ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n13/r1.claim: Asad's account omits the legendary embellishments that have obscured the story's or parable's meaning.

ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n14/r1.claim: The phrase literally says God increased or advanced the youths in guidance.

ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r2.claim: The Cave youths illustrate abandoning the world for faith through an allegory of death, resurrection, and spiritual awakening.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur'an tells the true details of the story, bypassing popular false accounts, to teach its wisdom rather than conceal a secret.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Calling them young directs the Prophet's contemporaries to follow their example, resisting their people's hostility with God's help.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.claim: Unable to profess or practice monotheism safely amid persecution, the youths left their people with their dog and sought refuge in the cave.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.claim: They prayed for mercy and a way out, hoping for God’s help; God accepted their prayer and caused them to sleep deeply for a long time.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r1.claim: The Quran stresses the Companions’ youth; some commentators say the young are more likely to follow prophets while elders cling to false religion.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r2.claim: Younger Quraysh members were more likely than their elders to follow the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r3.claim: Abraham’s youthful faith contrasts with his father’s idolatry; elsewhere community notables reject prophets.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r4.speaker: Q, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r4.claim: The word fatiyyah for youths is related to futuwwah, spiritual chivalry grounded in faith.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r5.speaker: Q, Su
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r5.claim: Futuwwah includes virtue, generosity, avoiding forbidden acts and harm, patience, truthfulness, freedom from hypocrisy, and detachment from worldly ties.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r6.claim: The term futuwwah later became associated with guilds that cultivated these virtues.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r7.claim: One interpretation of increased guidance is an increase in the youths’ faith.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r8.speaker: ST, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r8.claim: Another interpretation is greater understanding and discernment through faith, along with patience to endure separation from their people.

STUDYQURAN:18:13/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:13/r9.claim: The Quran says God increases tendencies already shown: disease for the unrepentant and faith for believers, including increased guidance.
